parsed.explanation: The state layer is comparatively benign: no facilities ban, a 2013 gender-identity public-accommodations law, penalty enhancements, marker change by provider letter, and a July 2026 'low-risk' classification. But the combined regime carries documented visitor-facing federal exposures that dominate: a February 2025 consular cable ordering refusal where documents cast doubt on sex (with fraud/lifetime-ineligibility referral), stopped X markers, reported blocked passports, and eight-plus foreign travel advisories; a federal bar on gender-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities; and federal corrections conversion-therapy policy plus documented immigration-custody abuse. Litigation is unresolved. Outing consequences reach major severity at entry and severe severity if detained, with partial but real state protections.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable directs officers to refuse cases where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex, and to weigh fraud/lifetime ineligibility; X markers stopped for new issues; trans travellers report passports blocked/confiscated; 8+ governments issued advisories over this.
entry_documents.protection: Civil-liberties union suit pending; existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Applies at the border regardless of the state's protective laws; state residence protections cannot reach consular adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted (from 2026) conversion-therapy-style policy: forced hair cutting, hormone removal, substitute psychiatric drugs; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men. No state placement policy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State law since 2015 lets inmates change birth-certificate names; state court/aid infrastructure functions.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained on entry (e.g., a refused visa or fraud question) enters the federal custody system, not the state's.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; nationally 9+1 units ban gender-identity facility use and 4 criminalise it, with one documented arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state has no facilities ban (equality map); its 2013 act covers public accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The federal rule reaches federal buildings inside this state despite the state's absence of a ban; state law cannot displace it.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders bar funding/promotion of gender-identity policies and subpoenaed under-19 hospital records; proposed rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 care. Adult visitor emergency-care denial not documented here.
care_services.protection: State bars gender-identity insurance discrimination (2016) and bans conversion therapy for minors including out-of-state referral (2018).
care_services.interaction: Federal funding levers can pressure providers the state otherwise protects.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National justice department reward memo and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy reference 'radical/radically pro-transgender' ideology; an executive order calls gender-affirming care 'mutilation'; a 2025 poll shows 66% support ASAB on documents, 69% on athletics.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute; state additional penalties for gender-identity-motivated violent crime since 2013; state LGBTQ+ commission (Jan 2025).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile federal framing raises outing probability and social friction while state penalty enhancements give some recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal executive order directs law enforcement to investigate schools and criminally prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; state-level gender-affirming-care bans exist in 27 units (this state's status for minors not stated).
minors_guardians.protection: State bans conversion therapy for minors and out-of-state referral; 2013 anti-discrimination act covers minors in public accommodations.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's exposure depends on school/contact settings, which a short visit rarely enters; state protections do not reach federal prosecution policy.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state figures on enforcement of the 2013 penalty enhancement or on reported anti-trans incidents; national statistics emphasise sexual-orientation bias; public opinion on documents is markedly hostile.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute plus state enhancement provide real, usable recourse if police act; no documented pattern of state-tolerated anti-trans violence here.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Silence on state enforcement is genuinely ambiguous rather than reassuring in this well-documented country.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, executive-order challenges and proposed health rules all unresolved; several orders enjoined; 2023 panic-defence bill disposition unknown; X-marker on licences dated only to 2020; state classified as 'low-risk' only in the weak sense of not targeting.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State act in force since 2013 with functioning legislature and courts; running legal-aid FAQ; national litigation capable of blocking measures.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work at state level but do not reach border adjudication or federal facilities, so outcome depends on which sovereign the traveller meets.

anchor_checks.comparison: Veluna imposes a national birth-sex toilet rule with courts routinely rejecting exclusion complaints and no exemption for foreign passports. Here the state has no facilities ban, its public-accommodations law operates, and several federal orders are enjoined. The federal facility bar and border cable keep this above 0.35, but they are narrower and litigable where Veluna's rule is settled and unremedied.

Ovessa shows repeated humiliating airport questioning only partially stopped despite discipline, with working tribunals elsewhere. Our dossier's border exposure is comparably recurring and partially corrected (litigation pending), but carries harsher potential consequences — fraud/lifetime-ineligibility findings, documented detentions, foreign advisories — plus custody conversion-therapy policy. Roughly similar tier, slightly heavier severity.

Ilvora has a dead-letter statute, acceptance, and ordinary courts enforcing compensation, with only an open question on nonbinary custody. Our case has operative federal exposures — an active consular refusal rule, a facilities bar, custody hormone removal — not dead letters. Documented hostile machinery plus unresolved litigation keeps us clearly below this reduced-risk level.

parsed.synthesis: Two sovereign layers interact uneasily. The state contributes genuine traveller-facing protections: gender-identity coverage in public accommodations since 2013, penalty enhancements, permissive marker change, no facilities ban, and a July 2026 'low-risk' label whose own wording is merely non-targeting. The federal layer adds exposures the state cannot offset: consular refusal and fraud referral on sex discrepancy (corroborated by eight-plus foreign advisories and reported detention of neighbouring citizens), a bar on gender-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities, and corrections/immigration custody practices reaching severe severity. Everyday street and service exposure in this state is therefore moderate, but entry screening and any detention scenario sharply raise it. Litigation is pending but has not produced relief, so paper challenge is not yet remedy. Travellers with consistent documents and no contact with federal facilities fare better; those stopped, detained, or travelling with a minor face materially worse outcomes.
